objectives.title: Find details in a short text

lessons.explanation: Use tú with a friend and usted for respectful singular address. Fixed expressions let you introduce yourself before learning whole verb paradigms.
commonMistakes: Do not use informal estás when this task asks for usted.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra lesson; grammatical rules checked against RAE references. Author review, 2026-10-30; no independent teacher audit.

lessons.explanation: Learn classroom instructions as useful fixed expressions. Identify the action and the body word; this is not a lesson in forming commands yet.
examples: Levanta la mano. = Raise your hand.
Abre el libro. = Open the book.
commonMistakes: A mano is a hand, not an arm. La mano is feminine despite ending in -o.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra lesson; grammatical rules checked against RAE references. Author review, 2026-10-30; no independent teacher audit.

lessons.explanation: Use es la una for one o’clock and son las with other hours. Add y + minutes; y media means half past. Numbers below are spelled as a single word when appropriate.
commonMistakes: Use la una, not las uno. Keep the accent in dieciséis and veintidós.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra lesson; grammatical rules checked against RAE references. Author review, 2026-10-30; no independent teacher audit.

stimuli.SpanishText: Hola. Me llamo Ana. Soy estudiante. En mi clase hay veinte estudiantes. Mi profesora se llama Elena. Por la mañana digo «Buenos días, profesora». Mi amigo Luis dice «Hola, Ana». La clase es a las ocho. En la mesa hay un libro y un lápiz. La profesora dice «Abre el libro, por favor». Yo digo «Gracias».
stimuli.provenance: Original fictional passage, authored for Palabra. Not a textbook reading.

stimuli.SpanishText: La clase es a las nueve.

culture.text: The pronoun vos is standard in much of the Río de la Plata region. This course starts with tú; hearing vos is a chance to notice another valid variety.
